`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The failed push shows why a pushed branch should be named in full. A worktree branch created with `-b <name> origin/master` takes `origin/master` as its upstream. With `push.default=upstream`, `git push origin <name>` then targets `master`. GitHub's required-check rule rejected it here, but `HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` avoids depending on that safety net.
- The `unit_diagnostics` text in the user docs is the kind of statement that goes stale silently. No test pins prose, and the queue's suites could not see it. The repository's rule of moving still-true decisions into guidance or docs when work finishes exists because a reader of the docs has no other way to learn that behavior changed.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
